executiveSummary: Surveillance reports from ECDC and PAHO covering late 2025 through May 2026 indicate multiple concurrent disease threats across the Americas and Europe. Avian Influenza A(H5N1) remains an elevated concern in the Americas with ongoing animal-to-human spillover risk flagged across multiple update cycles from November 2025 through March 2026. Mpox continues to circulate in the Americas region, and yellow fever has prompted a formal epidemiological alert in early 2026. Additional threats include resurgent pertussis, dengue, chikungunya, measles, hantavirus pulmonary syndrome, and seasonal respiratory virus co-circulation, reflecting a broad and complex multi-pathogen threat environment.
bottomLine: The Americas and Europe face a high-complexity multi-pathogen threat landscape dominated by H5N1 spillover risk, mpox transmission, yellow fever, and resurgent vaccine-preventable diseases.

threats.name: Avian Influenza A(H5N1)
signals: Multiple PAHO epidemiological updates issued November 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained H5N1 activity
Ongoing animal reservoir activity with documented human spillover risk across the Americas
Repeated update cycle suggests evolving and persistent threat rather than isolated events
threats.action: Activate enhanced zoonotic surveillance at animal-human interfaces; enforce PPE protocols for exposed agricultural and veterinary workers; coordinate with FAO and OIE for regional animal health response; prepare pandemic influenza contingency protocols

threats.name: Mpox
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued April 2026 confirming ongoing mpox circulation in the Americas
Sustained transmission requires continued alert status months after initial outbreak waves
Clade-specific risk assessment needed given global clade Ib emergence context
threats.action: Enhance case detection and contact tracing; expand vaccination coverage for high-risk populations; coordinate with CDC and national health authorities on clade characterization of circulating strains

threats.name: Yellow Fever
signals: Formal PAHO epidemiological alert issued March 2026 indicating active yellow fever risk
Alert-level designation implies cases or significant exposure risk identified in the region
Epizootics in non-human primates may signal geographic expansion of sylvatic transmission
threats.action: Verify vaccination coverage in at-risk populations; deploy rapid response teams to affected areas; strengthen entomological surveillance for Aedes and Haemagogus vectors; issue travel health advisories

threats.name: Dengue
signals: PAHO epidemiological update February 2026 confirming sustained high dengue burden
Americas Region has experienced record dengue years in recent cycles suggesting ongoing hyperendemicity
Multiple serotype co-circulation increases severe disease risk
threats.action: Intensify vector control operations; strengthen severe dengue case management capacity; promote community-based Aedes aegypti source reduction; monitor serotype shifts that may increase immune-naive population exposure

threats.name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
signals: Two separate PAHO alerts issued December 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained resurgence
Dual alert cycle over three months suggests ongoing epidemic rather than isolated cluster
Infant and unvaccinated population mortality risk is significant
threats.action: Audit vaccination coverage rates and identify under-immunized communities; implement cocooning strategy for newborns; consider maternal Tdap booster campaigns; investigate potential pathogen evolution or waning immunity drivers

threats.name: Measles
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 2026 for measles in the Americas
Region had achieved elimination status; any alert signals dangerous immunity gap
Importation and local transmission risk elevated in areas with declining vaccination rates
threats.action: Conduct emergency vaccination campaigns in identified low-coverage areas; strengthen airport and border health surveillance; ensure outbreak response protocols are activated within 24 hours of case confirmation

threats.name: Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued December 2025 for hantavirus pulmonary syndrome
HPS carries case fatality rates of 30-40% making even small cluster alerts significant
Seasonal rodent population dynamics may be driving increased human exposure
threats.action: Enhance rodent surveillance and control in affected communities; issue public health guidance on avoiding rodent contact; ensure hospitals in endemic areas have HPS case management protocols; investigate potential person-to-person transmission if Andes virus suspected

threats.name: Chikungunya
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 2026 indicating active chikungunya transmission
Alert status suggests geographic spread or case surge beyond baseline expectations
Co-circulation with dengue complicates clinical diagnosis and case management
threats.action: Strengthen vector surveillance and control for Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus; train clinicians on differential diagnosis from dengue; monitor for severe chikungunya presentations in vulnerable populations; assess geographic expansion risk

selectAgentSummary: Avian Influenza A(H5N1) is a BSL-3 select agent with pandemic potential and is flagged as Critical based on multiple PAHO epidemiological updates spanning November 2025 through March 2026, indicating persistent zoonotic activity across the Americas. Monkeypox virus (MPXV) is a BSL-3 select agent confirmed circulating in the Americas as of April 2026 and is flagged as Elevated. Yellow fever virus, also BSL-3, has prompted a formal PAHO epidemiological alert in March 2026. Hantavirus (Sin Nombre/Andes virus), BSL-3 agents, prompted a December 2025 PAHO alert for pulmonary syndrome cases in the Americas. These four BSL-3 detections collectively represent the highest-priority biosafety and public health concerns in the current surveillance period.

diseases: Communicable disease threats (multiple ECDC weekly reports)

amrSignals: No explicit AMR signals identified in available report titles; Bordetella pertussis macrolide resistance should be monitored given resurgence reports; broader AMR surveillance recommended within ECDC weekly threat reports which may contain detailed AMR data not captured in titles alone
emergingPatterns: Dual-cycle PAHO alerting for pertussis (December 2025 and March 2026) suggests a multi-month resurgence consistent with waning vaccine immunity dynamics seen globally
Simultaneous H5N1 animal alerts in November 2025 and March 2026 indicate sustained enzootic pressure with unresolved spillover risk rather than contained outbreak
Co-circulation of multiple arboviruses (dengue, chikungunya) creates diagnostic confusion and potential for overwhelmed vector control resources in the same geographic zones

Seasonal respiratory virus co-circulation alerts (RSV and influenza, January 2026) combined with Southern Hemisphere influenza season start alert (April 2026) indicate year-round respiratory threat burden across the Americas
ECDC weekly threat reports for five consecutive weeks (April-May 2026) suggest sustained elevated threat environment in Europe requiring continuous monitoring

Methanol poisoning alert (October 2025) and GLP-1 medication misuse alert (February 2026) indicate non-communicable and toxicological threats being tracked alongside infectious disease surveillance, reflecting broadened public health security mandate
